AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#635 @ 0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

Independent first T4 audit; **A/B/C 0/1/1**. Reviewed the complete 1,062-line current diff, D2 contract with the owner retention override, actual schema/session lifecycle, consent reader and service, deletion/append locking, tests and executed CI. Consent copy v4, append-only v3 re-consent behavior, caller-scoped hard deletion and late-append rejection are implemented; one real deletion/recovery acceptance defect remains. [Candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635).

### B-635-1 — Deleting today's chat prevents a fresh chat, and the acceptance fake hides the database constraint

`src/roman/roman.service.ts:173-205` retains the erased session's `(user_id,surface,day_key)` row. `openOrResumeSession:113-144` looks only for a live row, then attempts another insert with exactly today's key; `prisma/schema.prisma:6355-6359` enforces uniqueness over **all** rows, including tombstones. The insert throws P2002, its recovery lookup again excludes the tombstone, and the error escapes: after deleting a chat the user cannot open a new one for that surface until UTC midnight. This is inherited uniqueness behavior, but it is directly exercised by the deletion lifecycle this PR changes and contradicts the fresh-session acceptance claim in `test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts:316-324`. The test succeeds only because `makeFakePrisma`'s `romanSession.create:76-94` never enforces that unique index. [Session lifecycle](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L101-L205), [database invariant](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021/prisma/schema.prisma#L6350-L6359), [false-positive acceptance](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021/test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts#L316-L324).

**Minimal fix:** support a fresh same-day session without resurrecting the erased transcript or resetting the daily cap; preserve the deletion/append fence and ownership. For example, move erased-session rate accounting to a separate durable counter while releasing the active day key, or use an appropriately reviewed active-only uniqueness/session-generation scheme. Do not simply revive the tombstone, drop the rate-count accounting, or weaken its test. Add open → append → delete → open → append and concurrent-open/deleted-old-session-append regressions against the actual database uniqueness contract; keep the cap and foreign-user controls. [Affected deletion and rate accounting](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L173-L370).

Independent local probe copied the existing acceptance suite and changed **only its fake** to enforce the exact schema unique key. The existing “deleting a session hides it from resume (a fresh session opens)” test then failed with P2002 from `RomanService.openOrResumeSession:126`; no candidate production source was edited. Command: `heavy.sh env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/roman/audit-sol111-unique-constraint.spec.ts -t 'deleting a session hides'`; one failed reproduction, 20 deliberately filtered tests skipped, exit 1. The probe and log are retained under `ops/evidence/AUD-SOL-111/635-{unique-constraint-probe.spec.ts,probe.log}`. [Original acceptance and fake](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021/test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts).

### C-635-1 — legacy erased-session rollout inventory

Before serving the new retention promise, verify whether any pre-upgrade `deleted_at != null` sessions retain messages or subject context. They cannot be cleaned by the new DELETE because `getOwnedSession:153-157` rejects them before the transaction. If present, perform a separately authorized, scoped erasure/backfill with a populated fixture and preserve content-free rate accounting; alternatively provide evidence the set is empty. No production inventory was performed by this auditor, so this is a rollout qualification, not an asserted population count. [New delete predicate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/0a32b4fe99ffaed0b9aee3e82c69aef40012f021/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L148-L205), [retention contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635).

### Evidence and release boundaries

Prisma generation through heavy.sh passed. The ordinary exact-head targeted command `heavy.sh env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/ai-consent/ai-consent.service.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent.controller.spec.ts test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts test/roman/roman-streaming.spec.ts` passed **4 suites / 115 tests**; this does not close B-635-1 because their fake accepts the impossible duplicate. Exact-head CI actually passed **641 suites / 11,001 tests**, with 19 suites / 203 tests skipped and five todo, and all ten required gates including Schema parity are SUCCESS. [Executed CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/36973129101/job/110731147526).

The body correctly names #608's account-erasure dependency; deploy with/after #608, align mobile #310/#326 v4 and enable the ledger in the coordinated backend window. Local mocked tests and row-lock code analysis are not real PostgreSQL concurrency/device acceptance. Hold merge on B-635-1; no push, merge, workflow dispatch, flag, DB or production action. [Declared dependency and merge order](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635).

Fix round 1 for Sol's REQUEST CHANGES @ 0a32b4fe (comment 5955389344). Head is now e7f67576. It merges main e5d10bd8 (b012ae99), then adds dba3af5f and e7f67576.

- **B-635-1:** fixed with no schema change. In the same erase transaction, a delete moves the row to `day_key = erased:<session id>`, so the unique key `(user_id, surface, day_key)` is free and a fresh session opens the same day.
  - The shell stays deleted and holds no text and no subject context. Appending to the old session is still a 404.
  - The daily cap still counts the erased in-window user turns. They are now summed with a DB aggregate, so there is no 16-row bound.
  - The open path keeps the P2002 race recovery. If an unerased pre-upgrade row holds today's key, the open path erases that row and retries once.
- **C-635-1:** `RomanErasureSweep` (60 s after boot, then nightly at 04:00 UTC) erases every deleted row that still holds a calendar day_key: messages, subject context and key.
  - It uses a per-row compare-and-set, so it is safe on many machines, idempotent and bounded. It never touches live chats.
  - The cap does not double-count unerased rows.
  - I have no production access, so I cannot prove the inventory empty. The code handles any count.
- **Real uniqueness tests:**
  - The unit fake now enforces the real unique key over deleted rows, with a real Prisma P2002 and a negative control.
  - The new live spec `test/roman/roman-session-erase.live.spec.ts` (Postgres, full Prisma schema) covers: the negative control; open -> append -> delete -> open; 6 concurrent opens; a late append returns 404; a delete racing an append; the cap kept, with a foreign-user control; and legacy erase on open and by the sweep (idempotent).
  - The spec runs in a new final step of `mwb-3-live-tests`.
- **Local results:**
  - 10 suites / 188 tests passed (roman, ai-consent, module-graph).
  - Live spec on a throwaway PostgreSQL 18.6: 8/8.
  - Sweep spec: 7/7.
  - tsc exit 0, eslint 0, R75 OK.

PR body updated (tier header, Fix round rows B-635-1 / C-635-1). Requesting re-audit. I do not audit my own change.

AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-backend#635 @ e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

Re-audit after fix round 1. **A0 / B1 / C2.** Sol's B-635-1 and C-635-1 are both closed. One B stays open.

That B is mine. I found it at `0a32b4fe` but held the draft verdict when the operator re-queued this PR, so this is the first time it appears on the thread. It is numbered after Sol's IDs.

### Delta since 0a32b4fe
- **Merge `b012ae99` (main `e5d10bd8`) is pure.** Its tree `415d23e4` equals `git merge-tree --write-tree 0a32b4fe e5d10bd8`.
- **The fix commits are `dba3af5f` and `e7f67576`.** They touch only `src/roman/*`, `test/roman/*` and the mwb-3 live-spec step in `ci.yml`.
- **Merging with main `b9ee8e0a` is clean** (tree `730655fe`).

### Prior findings
- **Sol B-635-1 (a tombstone holds the same-day key, so a re-open gets P2002 and a 500): CLOSED.**
  - In the code, `eraseSessionInTx` (`roman.service.ts:212`) moves the row to `day_key = erased:<id>` inside the same compare-and-set transaction. `day_key` is `String` (text), so the 43-character key fits.
  - `openOrResumeSession` (`:120-156`) retries once after erasing an unerased holder. A second P2002 resumes the racing live row, and anything left over is a coded 503 `ROMAN_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE` with a next step.
  - The cap now sums erased shells in the database (`aggregate` restricted to the `erased:` prefix), so unerased tombstones are not counted twice.
  - Tests: the unit fake now enforces the unique key over all rows and throws a real P2002, with a negative control. The real-Postgres `test/roman/roman-session-erase.live.spec.ts` is **8/8 PASS** in [mwb-3-live-tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37031101104/job/110917832761).
- **Sol C-635-1 (pre-upgrade tombstones still hold transcripts): CLOSED.**
  - `RomanErasureSweep` runs 60 s after boot and at 04:00 UTC, and the open path also erases them.
  - The sweep's per-row compare-and-set (`deleted_at not null AND day_key = <old>`) is idempotent across machines, never touches a live row, and is bounded at 100 × 50 rows.
  - `roman-erasure.sweep.spec.ts` passes in build-and-test. This also covers my held C on the same point.

### B
**B-635-2: the client still cannot delete any Roman chat except today's, so the v4 copy "kept until you delete them" is false for every older conversation.**
- Sessions are one per (user, surface, UTC day) (`prisma/schema.prisma:6355`). The only routes are POST `/roman/sessions` (opens or resumes **today's** session), GET/POST `/roman/sessions/:id/messages` and DELETE `/roman/sessions/:id` (`roman.controller.ts:61, 71, 90, 171`).
- No route lists a caller's sessions or deletes them all, so a client cannot obtain the id of yesterday's chat. Mobile `romanApi.ts` calls exactly these four routes.
- Every chat older than today is therefore kept until account deletion only. That contradicts the copy this PR ships (`CLIENT_AI_CONSENT_PARAGRAPH`) and the OR-110-1 ruling that a client chat delete erases.
- **Minimal fix:**
  - Add `DELETE /roman/sessions`, which erases all of the caller's sessions on both surfaces. Loop `eraseSessionInTx` with guard `{ deleted_at: null }` over the caller's live rows, scoped by `user_id`. Return 204, including when nothing is left.
  - Optionally add `GET /roman/sessions`, listing the caller's own live sessions (`id, surface, day_key, message_count, last_activity_at`) so the app can show and delete chats one at a time.
- **Tests:**
  - a prior-day session and today's session are both erased (messages gone, subject context null, `erased:` key);
  - another user's rows are untouched;
  - the daily cap is not reset;
  - a live-spec case on Postgres.

### C (optional)
- **C-635-2: three sites throw an uncoded `NotFoundException('Roman session not found')`** (`roman.service.ts:168, 200, 389`).
  - Fix: add `{ code: 'ROMAN_SESSION_NOT_FOUND', message: 'This conversation no longer exists. Open Roman again to start a new one.' }`.
  - Consider making a repeat DELETE a 204, since the erased state the user asked for already holds.
- **C-635-3: the erase depends on BYPASSRLS.** `RomanMessage` has no DELETE policy for non-service roles, and both tables are FORCE RLS.
  - Under an RLS-enforced role, `deleteMany` would remove 0 rows silently while the route still returns 204.
  - Fix: inside `eraseSessionInTx`, assert after the delete that `tx.romanMessage.count({ where: { session_id } }) === 0`, and throw a coded error otherwise.

### Required checks at this exact head
- 10 of 10 required checks are SUCCESS: build-and-test (11,087 passed, including `test/roman/*` and `roman-erasure.sweep.spec.ts`), rls-floor-guard, rls-live-tests, mwb-3-live-tests, npm audit (high+critical, whole graph), CodeQL JS/TS, Banned cast tokens, build-sbom, danger, Schema parity.
- shellcheck fails only on the existing SC2015, which #639 fixes.

### Release items outside this diff (operator routing; unchanged from my held draft)
1. **No mobile UI deletes a Roman chat.** `softDeleteRomanSession` is unused on mobile main, #310 and #326. The v4 copy needs a mobile delete-chat affordance on top of the B-635-2 route.
2. **"or delete your account" needs #608.** It is true only once #608's account-erasure manifest is deployed.
3. **Ship order: #635 before mobile #310 and #326.** Those builds send `client-ai-v4`, while main's ledger is `client-ai-v3`, so they would get 409 CONSENT_VERSION_MISMATCH until #635 deploys.
4. **Data export (main) omits Roman chats**, which are now kept indefinitely. This belongs to B-EXPORT.

No push, merge, dispatch or production action by this auditor.

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#635 @ e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

Independent T4 re-audit; **A/B/C 0/2/3**. **B-635-1 closes**: erase atomically releases the all-rows unique day key without reviving content, open recovers a legacy holder and concurrent P2002, and erased turns remain in the daily cap. The actual PostgreSQL CI negative control and lifecycle/concurrency tests execute, rather than relying on the former permissive fake. [Fix round](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635#issuecomment-5956261388), [executed live CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37031101104/job/110917832761).

### B-635-3 — Per-row erasure failures bypass the promised alert and log raw ORM diagnostics

`RomanService.eraseUnerasedDeletedSessions:312-316` catches every failed row transaction, logs its raw `.message`, and returns a normal erased count. Consequently `RomanErasureSweep.run:54-64` never enters its safe-diagnostic/Sentry catch for those failures: a sweep can leave deleted chats unerased with no Sentry event, including a zero-result run that emits no completion log. Raw Prisma messages can contain query arguments; the repository already provides `safeDiagnostic` specifically to prevent that disclosure. [Actual per-row catch](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L282-L321), [outer wrapper](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman-erasure.sweep.ts#L52-L65), [existing safe diagnostic contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/observability/orm-diagnostics.ts).

**Minimal fix:** sanitize before logging or reporting, and report per-row failures or a sanitized partial-failure summary while continuing healthy rows; preserve failed rows for retry and make incomplete erasure observable. Test the real service's per-row catch, not only a wrapper double that throws from the whole service call. [Affected implementation and current wrapper tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L282-L321), [sweep tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/test/roman/roman-erasure.sweep.spec.ts).

The independent auditor-only probe calls the actual service plus wrapper with a known Prisma P2024 row-transaction failure and a **synthetic** private-diagnostic canary: `heavy.sh env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/roman/audit-sol2-erasure-failure.spec.ts`. Both assertions fail as expected: capture count is zero and the raw canary reaches Logger.error; **2 failed / 2 total, exit 1**. Candidate production source is unchanged; probe/log retained as `ops/evidence/AUD-SOL-111/635-q2-{erasure-failure-probe.spec.ts,probe.log}`. [Exercised service branch](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L300-L321).

### C-635-1 — Rollout completion remains a qualification

The new CAS sweep and on-open legacy recovery address the missing erasure mechanism, but the boot sweep is bounded to 100 rows × 50 batches, not an unbounded guarantee that “first start … clears every pre-upgrade row”; failures are skipped within a run and the next scheduled attempt is nightly. Retain the optional operator qualification: after old writers have drained, establish the remaining unerased-tombstone set is empty, or continue controlled batches until it is; correct the unconditional first-start comment. No production population count or production erasure was performed by this auditor. [Bounded loop](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.service.ts#L282-L321), [batch defaults](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.constants.ts), [first-start claim and schedule](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman-erasure.sweep.ts#L11-L49).

### Newly published parallel audit — carried findings

**B-635-2 remains open:** independently checked the controller has only today's open/resume and id-addressed message/delete routes, with no own-session list or erase-all route; therefore it does not provide a way to discover and erase yesterday's chat after its id is lost. Add an owner-scoped list/delete affordance or erase-all route, with previous-day, foreign-user, daily-cap and live PostgreSQL coverage; the paired mobile affordance remains required. [Controller route inventory](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.controller.ts), [parallel B-635-2](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635#issuecomment-5956763748).

**C-635-2/3 carried as optional:** replace the three uncoded session-not-found errors with a stable actionable code; make erasure verify zero remaining messages rather than silently relying on BYPASSRLS. These are the parallel audit's existing IDs, not new duplicates. [Actual uncoded branches and erase implementation](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/e7f67576fddfe77418b51a653d3492fcb43fba5f/src/roman/roman.service.ts), [parallel optional findings](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635#issuecomment-5956763748).

### Evidence and boundaries

Read the complete own diff, all prior audit comments, fix-round delta, retention/consent contract and final live-test CI addition; it adds a last step without weakening existing gates. Independently reconstructed the main merge tree `415d23e4b70250207065c29f41ebae8a54b18090`; before/after own zero-context patch IDs both equal `8fc8337812309cb132b33ace1c99b42ec2754cfd`. [Candidate history and changed files](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635).

Through heavy.sh, Prisma generation passed and `env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/roman/roman.service.spec.ts test/roman/roman-erasure.sweep.spec.ts test/roman/roman.controller.spec.ts test/roman/roman-streaming.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent.service.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent.controller.spec.ts test/ai-consent/ai-consent-dunning-lockout.e2e.spec.ts test/module-graph.spec.ts` passed **8 suites / 159 tests**. Exact-head required ten checks all SUCCESS; actual build CI passed **644 suites / 11,087 tests**, 20 suites / 211 skipped, five todo; the new PostgreSQL live suite passed **8/8** with no skipped cases. [Build execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37031101104/job/110917832961), [PostgreSQL execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37031101104/job/110917832761).

Hold merge on B-635-2/3; #608 account-erasure, mobile #310/#326 v4 and coordinated ledger activation remain release dependencies. No push, merge, dispatch, local DB, device or production action. [Declared dependencies](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/635).

**Fix round 2 @ c2688010** (from e7f67576; Opus AUDIT 5956763748, Sol AUDIT 5956842685). Merged main e867fe62 and 3bd6215b (merge commits 526036e8, c2688010, both clean). Fix commits 653a9bfb, 98af609e.

| Finding | Disposition | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| B-635-2 | Fixed. `GET /roman/sessions` (own live chats, keyset cursor, metadata only), `DELETE /roman/sessions` (every chat, both surfaces, every day, 204 even when none), `DELETE /roman/sessions/:id` (any day). New `RomanChatsController`, JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard, outside the chat flag, `no-store`. Cap never reset. Also: `?limit=30` was a 400 on the messages list (`@Type(() => Number)` added); that route is now `no-store`. | roman.service.spec B-635-2 block; roman-chats.controller.spec (Nest over HTTP, flag OFF); live: prior-day + today delete-all, other user untouched, cap kept, paging |
| B-635-3 | Fixed. Per-row failures go through `safeDiagnostic`, are counted (`failed`, `firstFailure`), stay for retry; the sweep sends one sanitized Sentry `RomanErasureIncomplete` summary and logs `erased= failed= remaining=` every run. | Sol's probe unmodified: 2/2 fail at e7f67576, pass now; sweep spec with the real service per-row catch |
| C-635-1 | Fixed. Follow-up run 60 s later while it makes progress; with no progress, 4 retries at 15 min then `RomanErasureStalled`. Comment corrected. Operator check (`remaining=0` or the count SQL) in `docs/roman-chat-deletion.md`. | sweep spec follow-up / retry / destroy cases |
| C-635-2 | Fixed. Coded 404 `ROMAN_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` everywhere; repeat delete 204, writes nothing; own legacy tombstone erased by id. | service spec C-635-2 block; live prior-day case |
